scope: Named foreign shareholders (≥1%) of five NIFTY 50 / SENSEX constituents in batch 8 (Sun Pharmaceutical Industries, Tata Consultancy Services, Tata Consumer Products, Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles, Tata Steel), from the latest available SEBI Reg. 31(1)(b) quarterly shareholding-pattern data. Four companies were checked against the primary filing opened directly from the company's own investor-relations site: Sun Pharmaceutical Industries (quarter ended 31.03.2026), Tata Consumer Products (30.06.2026), Tata Steel (30.06.2026) and Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles (30.06.2026, its first full quarter as an independently listed entity following the October 2025 Tata Motors demerger into TML Commercial Vehicles Ltd / renamed Tata Motors Ltd and Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles Ltd). Tata Consultancy Services could not be opened at its primary source within budget: tcs.com returned HTTP 403 to every request (WebFetch and curl, with and without a browser User-Agent and Referer header) on both the financial-statements index page and two guessed direct-PDF URLs (Jun 2026 and Mar 2025 quarters) — the domain appears to block this environment's proxy outright, not merely this one document — so TCS rests on screener.in's aggregate (tier reported), with the attempted primary URLs recorded in voids. Covers: the mandatory comparison set (BlackRock, Vanguard, NBIM/Government Pension Fund Global, GIC/Government of Singapore, Capital Group, Fidelity, Kuwait Investment Authority, ADIA, GQG Partners) tested against the four companies with primary data; LIC of India as the domestic control on all four; and the FPI/Institutions-(Foreign) aggregate percentages and quarter dates for every company, including TCS. The striking finding across all four primary filings opened is that no individual foreign FPI holder was named ≥ 1% in three of the four (Tata Consumer Products, Tata Steel, Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles) — only Sun Pharmaceutical had one, Norges Bank's Government Pension Fund Global at 1.06% — and none of the five companies in this batch has a foreign promoter (all four Tata companies are controlled by the wholly domestic Tata Sons Private Limited; Sun Pharma's promoter group is the Shanghvi family's domestic holding entities). Leaves out: adviser mandates, SEBI/RBI rule-change history and the Soros/OSF/World Bank narratives, out of scope for this batch file; any company outside the five named above.

symmetryCheck: Run identically across the 5 companies in this batch: LIC of India was found as a large, specifically-named domestic holder in all four companies where a primary filing was opened — 5.23% of Sun Pharmaceutical Industries, 8.23% of Tata Consumer Products, 6.37% of Tata Steel, 4.75% of Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles — in every case larger than any single named foreign FPI line in the same filing (where any foreign line was named at all). BlackRock/iShares, Vanguard, GIC, Capital Group, Fidelity, Kuwait Investment Authority, ADIA and GQG Partners were not found named ≥1% in any of the four companies checked with primary data. Norges Bank's Government Pension Fund Global (NBIM) was the sole exception, at 1.06% of Sun Pharmaceutical — smaller than LIC's stake in that same company (5.23%) by a factor of five. None of the five companies in this batch has any foreign promoter or FDI strategic stake at all (unlike ITC/British American Tobacco or Maruti Suzuki/Suzuki Motor Corporation documented in earlier batches): all four Tata companies share the single wholly-domestic promoter Tata Sons Private Limited (31.8–40.1% depending on company), and Sun Pharma's promoter group is the domestic Shanghvi-family holding entities (54.48%). The lens therefore produces, for this batch, an even starker version of the pattern already found in prior batches: the largest identifiable single shareholder in every company checked is either the domestic promoter or LIC, never a foreign passive fund, and in three of four companies no foreign holder is individually named at all.
